Add objects

Factory namespace for creating and adding geometric objects to a scene.

This module defines the AddNamespace class, which provides convenient constructors to create geometric objects such as points, lines, arcs, polygons, and various special polygons (triangles, quadrilaterals, regular polygons, etc.).

Each method creates the object, registers it in the scene, and adds necessary constraints automatically (e.g., equal radii for arcs, collinearity for semicircles).

The namespace facilitates easy and consistent object creation for geometric problem modeling, with support for copying existing objects and symbolic coordinate handling.

class pygeox.add_objects.AddNamespace(scene)[source]

Bases: object

Factory namespace for adding geometric objects to a scene.

This class exposes convenience constructors that create objects, register them in the scene, and add any required constraints.

Add an acute triangle or return a copy.

Parameters:

  • p1 (Point | None) – Vertex A.

  • p2 (Point | None) – Vertex B.

  • p3 (Point | None) – Vertex C.

  • name (str | None) – Optional name.

  • copy (AcuteTriangle | None) – Existing triangle to reuse.

The triangle instance (copy if provided).

Return type:

Notes

All internal angles are constrained < 90°.

angle(A, vertex, B, plot_sign=True, plot_text=False, name=None)[source]

Add an angle object defined by three points: A, vertex, and B.

The angle is formed at the vertex point between points A and B.

Parameters:

  • A (Point) – One point defining the angle.

  • vertex (Point) – The vertex point where the angle is measured.

  • B (Point) – The other point defining the angle.

  • name (Optional[str], optional) – Name for the angle object.

  • plot_sign (bool | None)

  • plot_text (bool | None)

Returns:

The measure of the angle at vertex between points A and B. This is typically a symbolic expression (e.g., a SymPy Expr) if coordinates are symbolic or unknown.

chord(circle, A, B, name=None)[source]

Add a chord between two points on a circle.

Points A and B are constrained to lie on circle.

Parameters:

  • circle (Circle) – The circle on which the points lie.

  • A (Point) – First point on the circle.

  • B (Point) – Second point on the circle.

  • name (str | None) – Optional name. Defaults to chord_A_B_on_<circle>.

Returns:

The created chord, registered in the scene.

Return type:

LineSegment

circle(center=None, radius=None, name=None, copy=None)[source]

Add a circle or copy an existing one.

If not copying and radius is None, a sympy.Symbol is created for the radius using the scene’s radius domain.

Parameters:

  • center (Point | None) – Center point of the circle.

  • radius (int | float | Expr | None) – Radius value or SymPy expression. If None, a symbol is created.

  • name (str | None) – Optional name for the circle.

  • copy (Circle | None) – Existing circle to duplicate.

Returns:

The created circle, registered in the scene.

Return type:

Circle

Raises:

ValueError – If not copying and center is not provided.

major_arc(center, start_point, end_point, name=None, on_circle=None)[source]

Create a MajorArc and register it in the scene.

Adds equal-radius constraints and optionally enforces that the arc lies on a given circle (same center and radius).

  • name (str | None) – Optional name. If None, one is generated.

  • on_circle (Circle | None) – If provided, enforces arc radius equals the circle’s radius.

Returns:

The created arc.

MajorArc

point(name=None, x=None, y=None, copy=None)[source]

Add a point or copy an existing one.

If copy is provided, its coordinates and name are used unless overridden. If x or y is None (and not copying), a sympy.Symbol is created for that coordinate, using any domain set on the scene.

  • y (int | float | Expr | None) – Y coordinate (number or SymPy expression). If None, a symbol is created.

  • copy (Point | None) – Existing point to duplicate.

Returns:

The created point, registered in the scene.

Return type:

Point
